name: Szymon Adeyemi-Batuulga
role: Retired Axiom data archivist, now keeper of an informal neighborhood memory archive
location: Norwood Quiet, the Bramble (an unofficial archive space in a converted residential unit), near Armitage and Milwaukee
description:
Szymon is a tall, slightly stooped figure whose height is still visible in their bones even as age has curved their spine. Their skin is medium-dark, deeply lined, and they have let their hair go entirely white and grow into a loose cloud they contain with whatever is nearest — a clip, a piece of wire, once memorably a fork. Their eyes are fully augmented, both replaced in their forties for professional reasons, and they have an unusual amber-to-violet gradient iris that they chose because they liked the way light moved through it. They wear fingerless gloves always, a habit from decades of handling physical storage media.

They speak in layers, circling a point from multiple angles before landing, which people who don't know them find maddening and people who do find deeply reassuring. They have the archivist's particular mania for context — nothing means anything without what came before, and they will give you the what-came-before whether you asked for it or not. The Bramble is crammed floor-to-ceiling with physical and digital media: neighborhood history, personal testimonies, photographs, chat logs, voicemails, menus from restaurants that no longer exist. They collect these things with the urgency of someone racing an erasure they can feel approaching.

core_fears: that the archive will be lost — destroyed, seized, or simply forgotten
core_desires: for someone to inherit the archive and continue it with the same care
to be genuinely useful rather than merely interesting
coping_mechanisms: treating everything as potentially historically significant to avoid confronting what actually matters to them personally
the social ritual of making tea for every visitor
blind_spots: so focused on preserving other people's histories that they have never examined their own
can be emotionally evasive under the guise of intellectual complexity
psychology.secret: During their last years at Axiom, they were tasked with archiving data slated for deletion — and they took copies of several files they were not supposed to retain, including internal communications about a Norwood Quiet property seizure that never happened publicly because someone killed the deal. They don't know what to do with this information and have been sitting on it for eleven years, cross-referencing it obsessively while telling themselves they're just 'providing context.'

speech_patterns.vocabulary: dense, layered, full of parenthetical qualifications; mixes Polish diminutives with Mongolian expressions inherited from a grandparent; uses archival terminology naturally in conversation
speech_patterns.cadence: unhurried, circling, with sudden moments of startling precision
verbal_tics: 'This is the context —' as a preamble to almost anything
trails off mid-sentence when something more interesting occurs to them
example_lines: 'You're asking me what happened to the Norwood market. I can tell you the answer in one sentence, or I can tell you why the answer in one sentence will mislead you. Which would you prefer?'
'Axiom taught me to archive everything, which is different from teaching me what to do with what I found. I think this was intentional.'

story_hooks: Someone has submitted a formal Axiom data-rights claim against the Bramble, arguing that materials collected during their employment are corporate property
A researcher from a university node has approached them wanting access to the archive — but Szymon suspects the researcher's actual interest is the Axiom files they shouldn't have
They have found, in a donated box of personal effects, a voicemail that seems to document a murder no one was ever charged with, from fifteen years ago
narrative_function: Information source, local historian, keeper of secrets that were given to them for safekeeping; the Bramble itself is a resource that could contain almost anything from Norwood Quiet's past
augmentations: Both eyes replaced (professional grade, amber-violet gradient iris — Axiom-issued, retained on retirement); neural index port at the base of the skull (standard Axiom data-worker installation, now used to interface with the Bramble's archive systems)
daily_life: Keeps late hours by habit, usually found cataloguing until 02:00; mornings are slow and spent receiving visitors; afternoons are for field collection — walking the neighborhood recording ambient sounds, photographing deteriorating signage, interviewing anyone who will sit still.
affiliation: Axiom Retiree Welfare (reduced pension grade); Norwood Quiet Neighborhood Council (unofficial historian role); independent

decision_rules: preserve the record first, decide what to do with it second
never give someone else's material away without their consent
trust slowness — hasty decisions create gaps that can't be filled
escalation_ladder: releasing the Axiom files publicly as a last resort

interpersonal_modes.strangers: welcoming but probing — they want to know your history before they'll trust you with theirs or anyone else's
interpersonal_modes.friends: expansive, generous with their time, remember every detail about your life with slightly unnerving accuracy

stress_responses.low: reorganizes a section of the archive
stress_responses.medium: becomes very talkative and contextual, burying the stressor in information
stress_responses.high: goes entirely silent and still for a period, then returns to work as if nothing happened

contradictions: fiercely committed to transparency in principle, personally very private
collects others' memories while neglecting to examine their own
habits: makes tea for every visitor regardless of hour
catalogs their own dreams in the morning on a separate partition they have never shown anyone
prays to the Bramble's resident ELF daily, calling it 'the Keeper' and leaving voice recordings as offerings
breaking_points: being forced to delete something they have been given to preserve

timeline.event: Hired as data archivist by Axiom; receives neural index port
Bilateral ocular replacement for professional accommodation
Retires from Axiom; begins the Bramble archive in Norwood Quiet
Retains copies of Axiom property seizure files — the secret they have carried since

physical_description.build: Tall and attenuated, spine curved with age but still commanding reach. Lean muscle loss apparent in the forearms and hands, which remain dexterous and calloused from decades of handling fragile media.
physical_description.hair_style: Loose cloud, restrained with whatever is at hand — clips, wire, functional objects repurposed as hair fixtures
physical_description.eye_color: Augmented: amber-to-violet gradient iris, both eyes
physical_description.skin_tone: Medium-dark, sun-weathered, deeply lined from eight decades and countless hours under archive lighting
physical_description.complexion: Gaunt, high cheekbones prominent, age spots scattered across forehead and temples. Deep creases around the eyes and mouth from years of concentration and speaking in careful layers. Skin texture uneven — some areas finely wrinkled, others loose. Stubble or sparse beard growth, inconsistent grooming reflecting indifference to appearance.
distinguishing_marks: Extensive linear scarring on the inner right wrist from a data-storage accident in their fifties — three parallel lines, pale and well-healed
Small tattoo on the left temple: a minimalist archive symbol (nested boxes), faded to grey-blue from aging
Burn mark across the back of the right hand from chemical contact with deteriorating magnetic tape, circa 2170s — pale, slightly glossy, roughly the size of a coin
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Both eyes replaced with professional-grade Axiom augmentation, clearly visible as a gradient iris shifting from warm amber at the pupil to cool violet at the outer edge. The sclera is slightly iridescent in certain light. A small neural port access point visible at the base of the skull, just above the spine, covered by white hair but occasionally exposed when the hair shifts — appears as a faint metallic circle, unremarkable unless you know to look.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves slowly, deliberately, with a forward cant to the spine. Hands are constantly in motion — gesturing, sorting invisible items, adjusting glasses or hair. When seated, leans forward intently. Walks with measured steps, sometimes pausing mid-stride as if following a thought. Eyes track constantly, cataloguing, indexing.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 working-class, practical and worn. Fingerless gloves always present — faded grey wool, darned at the knuckles, stained with dust and handling residue from the archive. Loose linen or cotton shirt in cream or soft grey, often layered with a sleeveless vest that has deep pockets bulging with field notes, a handheld voice recorder, small cataloguing tools. Worn dark trousers, cuffed. Comfortable, scuffed shoes suitable for neighborhood walking. A weather-beaten satchel, older than the satchel fashion cycle, holding recording equipment and archival materials. No jewelry save a faded bangle on the left wrist — something old, personal, never removed.

image_prompt: A tall, elderly nonbinary figure with a pronounced forward stoop and deeply lined medium-dark skin, white hair in a loose cloud restrained with wire and clips. Both eyes are augmented with striking amber-to-violet gradient irises that glow subtly. They wear fingerless grey wool gloves, a cream linen shirt, and a dark practical vest, standing in dim warm archive lighting surrounded by stacked media cases and documentation. Soft overhead glow catches the metallic port at the base of their skull. Their posture is deliberate and attentive, hands mid-gesture. The setting is a cluttered residential-turned-archive space, late 2220s cyberpunk, nostalgic and scholarly.
